evidence: At pinned HEAD 1603214845745174f5036ea79375198c7a44a1dd, the strongest concrete scenario supports the finding's code premise but does not contradict a stated document claim: commit seat.toml with name=b, then overwrite the checked-out file with garbage=true. The existing source test src/store/tests.rs:463-488 constructs exactly this case and expects the committed SeatRecord name to remain b (test inspected, not executed). Production reads agree: src/store/git.rs:110-128 resolves refs/heads/main and reads blobs from the selected commit; src/store/tree.rs:21-26 forwards CommitView reads to that revision; src/transcripts/mod.rs:172-176 selects store.head(), and src/transcripts/capture.rs:408-423 loads Graph through that view and inspects committed clone occupancy/session state. Graph::load at src/threads/effects.rs:55-65 loads teamspaces/seats/clones through TreeRead. The writer starts its overlay at committed head (src/writer/mod.rs:277-298), creates the next tree and CASes main (321-340), then attempts checkout projection (400-429); src/writer/worktree.rs:110-121 leaves differing disk content untouched and 220-221 records dirty/view status, while the writer can still return Committed at 438. Thus checkout divergence is real. However GRAPH_STATE.md:3 only says state lives in a dedicated Git repository containing TOML/Markdown and ignored operational state; :5 explicitly gives a rough layout; :31-43 names what the Git-tracked records store; :47 includes checkout status as local operational state. None asserts that uncommitted checkout contents are authoritative, that direct file edits become effective, or that committed operations require checkout success. The final artifact is an inventory of persisted state, not a reader/writer consistency contract or editing guide. Reproduction therefore yields no actual document-to-code mismatch within its stated scope. An authority sentence could be useful additional explanation, but omission alone does not demonstrate material harm caused by an inaccurate claim, and does not justify Should-fix under the requested descriptive-summary standard.
